package_info.why_malicious: The Slinger HTTP server contains a directory traversal vulnerability due to improper order of input sanitization and URI decoding, allowing attackers to access arbitrary files and execute arbitrary code via crafted network requests.

execution_context.file_location: Slinger HTTP server request handler (binary/firmware code)

malicious_snippets.code_language: HTTP (network protocol, interpreted by C/C++ server code)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the server receives a crafted HTTP GET request containing an encoded directory traversal sequence (/.%2e/), decodes the URI after sanitization, and accesses a file outside the intended web root, resulting in unauthorized file disclosure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior allows attackers to bypass intended directory restrictions and access sensitive files by encoding traversal sequences.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would strictly prevent access to files outside the web root, even with encoded traversal sequences. Here, sanitization is bypassed due to improper order of operations.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would involve serving only files within the web root, with all traversal attempts blocked.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (CGI script execution via HTTP request)
execution_context.file_location: Slinger HTTP server CGI handler (binary/firmware code)

malicious_snippets.code_language: HTTP (network protocol, interpreted by C/C++ server code)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the server receives a crafted HTTP GET request targeting the CGI handler, using encoded traversal and path separators to escape the CGI directory and execute an arbitrary system binary (/usr/sbin/logger) with attacker-controlled parameters, resulting in remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior enables attackers to execute arbitrary system commands by escaping the CGI directory using encoded traversal and path separators.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would restrict CGI execution to scripts within a designated directory, blocking traversal and encoded path manipulation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would only execute approved CGI scripts within the allowed directory.
key_indicators: Execution of system binaries outside CGI directory

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted HTTP request with encoded directory traversal sequences to the Slinger server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Unauthorized file disclosure from outside the web root.

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted HTTP request to the CGI handler with encoded traversal and path separators, escaping the CGI directory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote execution of arbitrary system binaries with attacker-controlled parameters.

behavioral_signatures: HTTP requests containing encoded directory traversal sequences (e.g., /.%2e/ or %2e%2e%2f)
Access to files outside the web root or CGI directory
Execution of system binaries via CGI handler with encoded paths
file_indicators: Access attempts to sensitive files (e.g., /private/secret.txt) via HTTP
CGI handler invoked with encoded traversal in script path
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with %2e (.) and %2f (/) in the path
Unusual GET requests targeting CGI handler with encoded paths
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor HTTP server logs for requests containing encoded traversal sequences (/.%2e/, %2e%2e%2f, etc.) and attempts to access files or execute binaries outside the designated web root or CGI directories. Alert on any CGI execution requests with encoded path manipulation. Use file access monitoring to detect unauthorized reads or executions triggered by the HTTP server process.
